newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile stocks rally to feverish close on rate rumor.
newsitem.headline: Chile stocks rally to feverish close on rate rumor.

text.p: Rumors of a Central Bank rate cut sent Chilean stocks into a New Year's buying frenzy, pushing the blue chip index up nearly three percent at the close, brokers said.
Central Bank officials had no comment on the rumors, which gathered force in afternoon trade and lasted till the close.
The blue-chip IPSA index finished 2.76 percent higher to 103.22 points. The all-share IGPA ended up 1.38 percent to 4980.10 points on strong volume of 111 million shares traded.
"Everyone is buying. The rumors get stronger and stronger," said one broker.
Buying was accelerated by bargain-hunting after the market's sag in the final weeks on 1996, particularly in the electrical sector, said brokers.

Some brokerages timed their buying to take losses in 1996 and were now buying again, adding to the rise, said one broker. A few positive brokerage recommendations also contributed to bullish sentiment.

Central Bank rate announcements usually come on Friday afternoons after the stock exchange closes. But forty-five minutes after the final bell, there was still no comment, official or otherwise, from Central Bank officials.
Foodmaker Iansa closed 1.1 percent higher on a Santander buy recommendation at 93 pesos, and steelmaker CAP rose six percent to 900 pesos.
But electrical stocks were the star of the show, recovering after the beating they took in late 1996 on concerns over the effects of drought and long-term competition on their earnings.
Chilgener rose 6.3 percent to 2,280 pesos and Endesa climbed four percent to 219 pesos. Enersis was up three percent to 231 pesos.
